podcast.title: Difficult Recording of Second Album
podcast.body: The second Yazoo album was recorded under strained circumstances, with Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet literally not speaking to each other. Clarke would work on the music, leave the studio, and then Moyet would come in to record vocals, with messages about retakes left through the recording team. "el segundo disco, a pesar de ser increíble, era grabado con los dos miembros de la banda sin literalmente dirigirse la palabra."

podcast.title: Pioneers of 1980s Techno Pop
podcast.body: Yazoo is mentioned as one of the groups central to the techno pop sound of the 1980s, alongside bands like Depeche Mode, Human League, and Visage. This era saw widespread adoption of synthesizers in popular music. "And this brings us to the techno pop sounds of the 1980s, to Pesh Mode, Human League, Yazoo, Visage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Vince Clark's Post-Depeche Mode Project
podcast.body: After leaving Depeche Mode, Vince Clark formed Yazoo, a project that achieved a series of hits and enjoyed considerable success for a period. "There was a group called Yazoo, what a series of hits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vince Clark's Departure (December 1, 1981)
xref.body: On December 1, 1981, chief songwriter Vince Clark left Depeche Mode, believing the group had little future and that he could achieve greater success on his own. While his subsequent projects like Yazoo and Eurasia had hits, Depeche Mode's overall album sales (over 50 million) ultimately surpassed his post-band career. "The date was December 1, 1981. The first member and chief son writer Vince Clark decided that he wanted out. Why? Well, he didn't think the group had much of a future."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dolby Cafe Breakfast Challenge (August 21, 2018)
xref.body: On August 21, 2018, in Cliftonville, Margate, the "very skinny" Pete Doherty, who is six feet three inches tall, successfully completed the Dolby Cafe's "eating challenge" breakfast. The meal, served on a toilet-seat-sized plate, included four eggs, four strips of bacon, four sausages, hash browns, onion rings, beans, a quarter-pound hamburger patty, french fries, two thick slices of toast, and bubble and squeak, which he finished in under 20 minutes, earning a free meal and national news coverage. "And he was successful, washing everything down with some coffee, and with a strawberry flavor drink called Yazoo, which sounds lovely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding Mute Records
xref.body: Using the profits from "Warm Leatherette," Daniel Miller established his own independent record label, Mute, dedicated exclusively to guitar-less music, which later introduced artists like Depeche Mode, Erasure, and Yazoo. "He took the profits and founded his own independent record label devoted entirely to guitar less music. He called the label Mute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneers of 1980s Techno Pop
xref.body: Visage is highlighted as a key act in the development of 1980s techno pop, a genre characterized by the pervasive use of synthesizers. They are grouped with other influential bands like Depeche Mode, Human League, and Yazoo. "And this brings us to the techno pop sounds of the 1980s, to Pesh Mode, Human League, Yazoo, Visage."
